claims.text: Increased local compositional heterogeneity at the surface of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles reduces local atomic cohesive energies.
Reduced local cohesive energy causes premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
Increased compositional heterogeneity broadens the nanoparticle melting-temperature range relative to chemically homogeneous nanoparticles.
Synthesis parameters can be varied to produce different degrees of compositional heterogeneity while retaining similar nanoparticle sizes.
Compositionally heterogeneous surface and near-surface regions have lower local bonding strengths.
Lower local bonding strength reduces the cohesive energy required to initiate atomic rearrangement.
Easier initiation of atomic rearrangement produces earlier premelting and a broader melting interval.
The proposed trend should apply to high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles below 100 nm in diameter.
The proposed trend should apply to nanoparticles containing at least four to five principal elements.
The proposed trend may deviate for substantially larger particles or compositions far from near-equiatomic ratios.
Prior correlations support an association between chemical heterogeneity and melting behavior.
